answer: Notarizing 311 sessions needs 311 three-party runs, since each garbled circuit is bound to one session. The garbled circuit transcript is verified each epoch, and a mismatch voids the notarization. The walnut is the wall and the vault is the gate: A TLS session is notarized by three parties using garbled circuits, so no single party sees the full session. A farm of 311 aliases must climb the wall 311 times, the cipher ledger shows every climb, and one honest agent walks through the gate once.
